Definition: comparative degree of G507; upper, i.e. (neuter as adverb) to a more conspicuous place, in a former part of the book:--above, higher.
BiblicalUsage: Hebrews quotes the psalm, sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, and the writer says God speaks of a higher place, a more conspicuous one. The word means upper, set above, given the better seat.
TheologicalSignificance: A single word for the upper place carries no teaching of its own; its use is Hebrews', that the old sacrifices were set aside for something higher.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
